newsitem.title: FRANCE: Interpol sets crackdown on crimes against children.
newsitem.headline: Interpol sets crackdown on crimes against children.

text.p: The international police organisation Interpol is expected to ask member states to launch a global crackdown on crimes against children at its 65th general assembly next week in Antalya, Turkey.
Delegates from the 176 member states will discuss a resolution urging greater international cooperation against such crimes, Interpol said in a statement on Thursday.
International outrage has been mounting against crimes against children since the recent discovery of a child sex ring in Belgium, believed responsible for killing at least four young girls.
So far 13 people have been charged in connection with the deaths in Belgium, and a team of more than 350 police remain on the case, seeking at least seven other missing children.
The Interpol meeting is also expected to focus on environmental crimes, fake credit cards and cross-border crimes, said the organisation, whose international headquarters are in Lyon, central France.
